title: How to Control Diagram Layout in Mermaid
summary: Control Mermaid 12 diagram layout with ELK or dagre. Set global and per-diagram options, tune ELK, and restore pre-12 rendering when upgrades change diagrams.
body_markdown:
In Mermaid 12, the` layout` config key decides the layout engine: ELK is the default for most graph diagrams, and you set` layout: dagre` in front matter or` mermaid.initialize()` to get the previous engine back.


You upgraded, rebuilt the docs site, and a flowchart nobody has touched now has a different shape and different colours. A diagram type section like` flowchart: { defaultRenderer: ... }` from an older answer won’t fix it.


This article covers what changed, where to set the layout, which setting takes priority, how to tune ELK, and why a revert can appear to do nothing. For flowchart basics, see[creating flowcharts for workflows](https://blog.openreplay.com/creating-flowcharts-to-enhance-workflows/) .


## Key Takeaways


- Since Mermaid 12.0.0, flowchart, state, class, entity relationship, requirement, use case and agentflow diagrams that don’t set a layout are arranged by ELK instead of dagre.
- ` layout: dagre` brings back the old arrangement but not the old appearance. The full pre-12 rendering needs` layout: dagre` ,` theme: default` and` look: classic` .
- Front matter or a directive on a diagram overrides` mermaid.initialize()` , so a site-wide dagre setting does nothing for a diagram that picks its own layout.
- ` defaultRenderer` was removed from the flowchart, class and state config sections in Mermaid 12. Use the top-level` layout` key instead.
- The tiny build doesn’t include ELK and falls back to dagre unless you add` @mermaid-js/layout-elk` .


## What Changed in Mermaid 12?


Starting with Mermaid 12, a diagram that doesn’t specify a layout is arranged by ELK instead of dagre. That means an unchanged diagram can come out a different shape after you upgrade. The[Layouts configuration page](https://mermaid.js.org/config/layouts.html) lists seven diagram types that now default to ELK: flowchart, state, class, entity relationship, requirement, use case and agentflow. ELK ships with the main package and registers itself automatically. Mindmaps still use cose-bilkent by default, and tidy-tree comes from the separate` @mermaid-js/layout-tidy-tree` package.


The[mermaid@12.0.0 release notes](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases/tag/mermaid%4012.0.0) also describe a second change. The default theme is now redux-color and the default look is now neo, for the wider set of diagram types listed in the[theming page’s per-diagram defaults](https://mermaid.js.org/config/theming.html) . So a v12 diagram can look different for two separate reasons: the layout engine changed, and the theme and look changed.


## Where Do You Set the Layout: Front Matter, initialize() or Per-Type Config?


You can set the Mermaid layout on one diagram or for every diagram on a site. You can also scope theme and look to a single diagram type. When settings conflict, the most specific one wins.


Scope Where Syntax Beats


One diagram Front matter or directive` config: layout: dagre` Everything below


All diagrams` mermaid.initialize()` top level` { layout: 'dagre' }` Type and global defaults


One diagram type Built-in type default (set by Mermaid) Global default


Everything Global default (set by Mermaid) Nothing


The 12.0.0 release notes give the resolution order as: front matter or directive first, then` initialize()` , then the diagram type’s default, then the global default.


Here is how to revert a single diagram completely:


```text
---
config:
layout: dagre
theme: default
look: classic
---
flowchart LR
Request --> Auth{Valid token?}
Auth -->|yes| Handler
Auth -->|no| Reject
```


Site-wide, the first call below changes the engine and nothing else, so the new colours stay. The second call brings back the whole pre-12 rendering:


```text
mermaid  .  initialize  ({   layout  :   '  dagre  '   });


mermaid  .  initialize  ({   layout  :   '  dagre  '  ,   theme  :   '  default  '  ,   look  :   '  classic  '   });
```


Mermaid 12 also lets you scope` theme` ,` look` and` layout` to one diagram type, inside that type’s config section. A scoped value beats a global one set in the same place. To switch every diagram to dagre but bring back the old appearance for class diagrams only, keep` layout` at the top level and put` theme` and` look` in the` class` section, as the[class diagram page](https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/classDiagram.html) shows:


```text
mermaid  .  initialize  ({
layout  :   '  dagre  '  ,
class  :   {   theme  :   '  default  '  ,   look  :   '  classic  '   },
});
```


Front matter always beats` mermaid.initialize()` . Suppose a site sets` layout: 'dagre'` site-wide and one diagram declares` layout: elk` in its front matter. That diagram renders with ELK.


## When Does the Mermaid ELK Layout Help and How Do You Tune It?


Use ELK for large or crowded diagrams. Keep dagre when a small diagram already looks fine. The Mermaid docs pitch ELK for big, intricate graphs, and dagre is still available as the long-standing layered layout. If your diagrams rendered well before the upgrade, reverting to dagre is a reasonable choice.


The[syntax reference’s layout section](https://mermaid.js.org/intro/syntax-reference.html) documents several ELK tuning keys, including these.` mergeEdges` combines parallel edges.` nodePlacementStrategy` accepts` SIMPLE` ,` NETWORK_SIMPLEX` ,` LINEAR_SEGMENTS` or` BRANDES_KOEPF` , and` BRANDES_KOEPF` is the default under the` default` preset.` nodePlacementAlignment` sets the Brandes-Koepf alignment (for example` BALANCED` or` NONE` ). When you leave it out, the alignment comes from the preset.


```text
---
config:
layout: elk
elk:
mergeEdges: true
nodePlacementStrategy: NETWORK_SIMPLEX
---
flowchart TD
Build --> Test --> Deploy
Build --> Lint --> Deploy
```


Diagrams that already used ELK before v12 can change too, because balanced Brandes-Koepf placement is now the default. The[ELK preset schema](https://mermaid.js.org/config/schema-docs/config-properties-elk-properties-preset.html) lists four` preset` values:` legacy` ,` default` ,` modelOrder` and` depthFirst` . It describes` depthFirst` as the previous default and says` legacy` reproduces how ELK rendered before presets existed.


ELK output has also changed within 12.x:


- [Mermaid 12.1.0](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases/tag/mermaid%4012.1.0) added` orientFeedbackEdges` , which is on by default. An edge running from a node that a subgraph feeds back into that subgraph is now routed downstream instead of around the subgraph.
- [Mermaid 12.2.0](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases/tag/mermaid%4012.2.0) stopped ELK from straightening an edge terminal when doing so would put a label over another edge.


```text
config  :
layout  :   elk
elk  :
preset  :   legacy
orientFeedbackEdges  :   false
```


## Which ELK Variants and Per-Subgraph Algorithms Can You Use?


Besides` layout: elk` , the Mermaid Layouts page lists six ELK variants you can use as` layout` values:` elk.stress` ,` elk.force` ,` elk.mrtree` ,` elk.sporeOverlap` ,` elk.box` and` elk.rectpacking` .


```text
---
config:
layout: elk.mrtree
---
flowchart TD
Root --> API
Root --> Web
API --> Workers
```


According to the[12.0.0 release notes](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/releases/tag/mermaid%4012.0.0) ,` elk.box` and` elk.rectpacking` place nodes but don’t route edges, so their edges are drawn as straight lines from centre to centre.


A single subgraph can choose its own algorithm with` @{ algorithm: ... }` . The same release notes list the accepted values as the six variants plus` elk.layered` and` elk.radial` . They also say two things about this override: Mermaid ignores unsupported values with a warning, and it uses the inherited algorithm instead whenever edges cross the subgraph’s boundary.


## Why Isn’t My Layout Fix Working?


Most failed reverts come from one of five causes. Check them in this order:


1. **You still set` defaultRenderer` .** The[flowchart syntax page](https://mermaid.js.org/syntax/flowchart.html) notes that it was removed from the flowchart, class and state sections in v12. Use` layout` instead.
2. **You set only` layout: dagre` .** The redux-color theme and neo look are still active. Set all three keys.
3. **Front matter overrides your` initialize()` .** Remove` layout` from that diagram’s front matter.
4. **A layout name is misspelled or unregistered.** The release notes say Mermaid falls back to dagre with a warning instead of throwing an error. Check the console.
5. **You’re on the tiny build.** See the next section.


Moving off` defaultRenderer` is a one-line change:


```text
// Before (removed in v12)
mermaid  .  initialize  ({   flowchart  :   {   defaultRenderer  :   '  elk  '   }   });


// After
mermaid  .  initialize  ({   layout  :   '  elk  '   });
```


If your docs platform hasn’t moved to v12 yet, these keys may still behave the old way. Check the platform’s own documentation.


## Why Does the Tiny Build Fall Back to dagre?


The tiny build of Mermaid leaves ELK out, so any diagram that asks for ELK there renders with dagre. The` @mermaid-js/layout-elk` package is still published for this case. Follow the registration steps in the[ELK and the tiny build](https://mermaid.js.org/config/usage.html#elk-and-the-tiny-build) section of the usage docs. On the normal build, existing` registerLayoutLoaders` calls keep working but are no longer needed, and you can delete them.


## Conclusion


A diagram that changed after the Mermaid 12 upgrade almost always has two causes: the ELK layout engine and the new theme and look. Decide what you want back. If you only want the old shapes, set` layout: dagre` . For the full pre-12 rendering, set` layout: dagre` ,` theme: default` and` look: classic` . Then search your config for any leftover` defaultRenderer` settings and any front matter that overrides your site-wide choice.


## FAQs


Does the flowchart-elk diagram keyword still work in Mermaid 12?


Yes. The Mermaid 12.0.0 release notes say flowchart-elk still works as an explicit diagram keyword. The defaultRenderer option is the part that changed. Mermaid ignores it rather than rejecting it, so a config that still sets it throws no error but has no effect. A diagram that relied on a flowchart defaultRenderer value of 'elk' for its ELK layout should set layout: elk instead.


Does bundling ELK make Mermaid 12 larger to load?


Only the single-file build grows noticeably. In the ESM builds, ELK is a separate chunk that loads only when a diagram uses it. The 12.0.0 release notes say the IIFE build, mermaid.min.js, inlines ELK and grows by roughly 500 kB gzipped. The tiny build leaves ELK out, stays the same size, and lays out ELK requests with dagre.


Can I set ELK tuning options site-wide instead of in each diagram's front matter?


Yes. elk is a top-level property in the Mermaid config schema, so you can pass it to mermaid.initialize() next to layout, for example layout: 'elk' with an elk object containing mergeEdges: true and nodePlacementStrategy: 'NETWORK_SIMPLEX'. A %%{init}%% directive accepts the same elk object for one diagram. Front matter on an individual diagram still overrides the site-wide values.
